Name: CRR - Ability to Modify Rules and Merge to production
Description: DESCRIPTIONAs a compliance analyst/manager, I want the functionality to modify rules in Sandbox and I am able to implement the changes into production to get desirable results. This feature enables users to trigger backend logic that merges sandbox-configured CRR rules into the production environment upon clicking the “Implement” button. It supports the identification, transformation, and production-level application of all sandbox modifications to Risk Elements, Risk Categories, Risk Rules, Rule Sets, and Rule Set Settings. Metadata changes including names, descriptions, weightings, default multipliers, applicability, value types, and advanced rule mode states must be persisted. The system must also support deletion logic—removing configurations from production if deleted in sandbox. Changes are versioned and stored in an auditable manner, though no user-facing audit interface is within scope. Users currently have the ability to create multiple different versions of the same scope, which causes duplicity and ultimately confusion in maintaining multiple CRR assessments.2. Users need to Enter risk thresholds repeatedly over and over again even though user research has shown that the same thresholds which are applicable to the Enterprise CRR have been used 99% of the times.3. Reposition Risk thresholds definition at a CRR Level instead of a market level to reduce time spent in create an assessment.3. Remove option to setup threshold overrides as whatever changes would be made to CRR Thresholds would be made at an enterprise level across all assessments at once in the future.4. Description: Feature DescriptionAs a Compliance Analyst/Manager, I want to perform a discovery and analysis of Event-Based Rule Triggers, where the system automatically triggers a rescoring process when specific variables change in source systems so that we can determine the feasibility, integration points, and requirements for implementing event-based rescoring within the CRR framework.Benefit to Business    •    Automates risk rescoring when critical data variables change, reducing manual interventions.    •    Improves risk assessment by ensuring that changes in customer attributes trigger a risk reevaluation.    •    Enhances accuracy and compliance by integrating with DAM (Data Access Manager) for event ingestion.Discovery ObjectivesThe CRR Tech Team will analyze the following aspects of Event-Based Rule Triggers:Understanding the Event-Based Rescoring Flow:    •    How DAM generates and sends event notifications when critical variables change.    •    What specific data variables trigger a rescoring event (e.g., geography, income level, risk profile updates).    •    How the CRR system consumes and processes these events.Validating Event Processing Logic:    •    Analyzing how the event-driven architecture aligns with current rescoring workflows.    •    Identifying latency and real-time processing requirements for event-based rescoring.Defining the Integration Between DAM and CRR:    •    Reviewing RTF Event specifications for event ingestion from DAM.    •    Evaluating message formats and payload structures for event triggers.User ScenariosReceiving an Event from DAM and Triggering RescoringDAM sends an event notification to the CRR system.CRR detects if the variable will affect customer risk scoringThe CRR system receives and validates the event payload.If the event is valid, the system initiates a rescoring process for impacted customer segments.The updated risk score is stored and logged in the CRR system.Handling Event Processing ErrorsIf DAM sends an incorrect or incomplete event payload, the CRR system logs the error and does not process rescoring.If CRR is down or unable to process the event, the system queues the event for retry.If an event does not meet the rescoring threshold criteria, the system ignores the event but logs it for auditing.Non-Functional RequirementsThe CRR system must handle event failures gracefully, logging errors and queuing retries.The system must support high-volume event processing with minimal latency.The event ingestion mechanism must validate all incoming data structures before triggering rescoring.The system must log all processed events for auditing and compliance tracking.DependenciesSome support might be required from DAM for integration: US5641504Issues/RisksPlaceholderOut of Scope    •    The final implementation of event-based rescoring is not part of this feature; this is for discovery and analysis.    •    This feature does not include real-time alerts for changes beyond the scope of DAM events.
